entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
=
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Mukesh Kumar Thakur, Advocate
 For the Respondent/s : Mr.Rishi Raj Sinha (Sc19)
 Mr. Saurabh Kumar, Ac to Sc-19

For the Nhai : Mr. Amarjeet, J. C. to Sriram Krishna, Advocate
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Dr. Anshuman
 Oral Judgment
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the National Highways Authority of India.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner is directed to implead the National Highways Authority of India through its official as party respondent in the present case, during course of the day.

3. The petitioner has filed the present petition with a prayer to enhance the compensation amount of the land which Patna High Court CWJC No.5849 of 2023 dt.15-09-2023 has been acquired for construction of NH-227A.

He further submits that the land of the petitioner is situated adjacent to SH- 73 which has been switched over under NH-227A and for the purpose of expansion, his land has been acquired and the petitioner is primarily interested in enhancing the compensation amount.

4. Learned counsel for the National Highways Authority of India submits that notice under Section 3E of the National Highways Act, 1956 has been issued at the level of the District Land Acquisition Officer, Siwan, therefore, the only remedy available to the petitioner to file an application under Vijay Kumar Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63008991/
1 Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
5.

entities.text: Vijay Kumar Singh vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the State submits that there is no applicability of Section 73 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 in the present case.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
6. In this view of the matter, since there is already a statutory remedy available against the notice impugned, this writ petition stands disposed of granting liberty to the petitioner to raise his grievances before the appropriate forum as indicated in Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act,
1956 within four weeks from today.
Patna High Court CWJC No.5849 of 2023 dt.15-09-2023 5.
With the aforesaid observation and direction, the present writ petition stands disposed of.

(Dr. Anshuman, J) Ashwini/-
